52 54 00 [6e 55 f4] 00 (these vary) seem to repeat a lot on the signal

Packets of interest start with CTFS, this would correspond to the hex digits

43 54 46 53

I can't trust that the first bytes sent are the header so I will look for CTFS, 
then read from there.

43 54 46 53 00 08 02 00 01 5b f0 82 fe 00 00 00

43 54 46 53 00 05 02 00 01 c9 18 e4 dc 00 00 00

Conveniently there are 2 packets which seem to be adjescent that fulfill this,
we can translate the entire section to be safe, though it is safe to assume the
header ends at 000 and doesn't follow the structure of a normal header file

Network order = big endimion = most significant byte first = normal

0x 00 07 = sequence number 7
0x 02 00 = 512, this corresponds to the length of the gap between CTFS packets, so we
           have a full example packet header

However when accounting for the 512 bytes this section is actually 528 bytes, accounting
for the header that we know, this leaves

01 ab 82 42 2d 00 00 00

Suggesting a 16 bit header

4 bytes left before 00 00 00 could correspond to doc type (e.g. PDF)?

Nevermind, putting them in a converter shows that they are Decimal values, idk what they are

Lets instead look for "%PDF", nevermind "PDF" (50 44 46)
3 results, nothing for the lowercase version
